resources.string: Enter %1$s on your device to connect
On iPhone or iPad, open Control Center and choose Screen Mirroring → “%1$s”. On a Mac, use Screen Mirroring in Control Center. In apps, tap the AirPlay button.
Choose Disconnect to stop, or stop AirPlay on your device.
The name your iPhone, iPad and Mac show in Screen Mirroring and the AirPlay menu. By default it follows this TV’s own name.
Stop the current session with %1$s and return to what you were watching.
Resolution, codec, refresh rate, latency, audio sync, passthrough, PIN and diagnostics.
Disconnects everyone and re-announces this TV on the network. Use it if a device can’t find the TV.
Saved. The receiver restarted; reconnect to use the new setting.
Saved. Applies from the next stream.
Settings for people who like control. Every option explains itself here when selected.
Press ◀ ▶ to change. Press OK to step through options.
The largest picture senders are told they can use. Auto picks the highest your TV can decode smoothly. Lower it on weak Wi-Fi for fewer stutters. Takes effect when a device next connects.
Auto offers HEVC (needed for 4K) and H.264, and the sender picks. H.264 Only is the most compatible and limits mirroring to about 1080p.
The display rate reported to senders. Match it to your TV’s mode (usually 60 Hz, or 50 Hz in PAL regions) for the smoothest motion.
Caps mirrored frames per second. 30 fps halves bandwidth and helps on congested networks; 60 fps is smoother for games and scrolling.
How much video is buffered before display. Low suits games and presentations; Smooth hides Wi-Fi hiccups at the cost of delay.
Turn on if the edges of the mirrored screen are cut off. Tells senders to keep content inside a safe area.
Off keeps the TV silent during Screen Mirroring, for example during a presentation while sound stays on your device.
Fine-tunes lip sync in 10 ms steps. Use + if sound arrives before the picture, − if it arrives after. Press OK to reset.
During AirPlay video playback, send Dolby/DTS audio untouched to a connected soundbar or AV receiver instead of decoding it on the TV.
Plays HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision video in HDR when the stream and your TV support it. Turn off if HDR content looks washed out.
Switches the TV’s refresh rate to match the video (for example 24 fps films) to avoid judder. Seamless Only avoids switches that blank the screen.
With On-Screen PIN, a new device must enter a 4-digit code shown on the TV the first time it connects. It is remembered afterwards.
Shows resolution, codec, frame rate, bitrate and dropped frames on top of the stream.
Restores every setting on this screen to its default. Your AirPlay name is kept.
Auto (H.264, no HEVC on this TV)
Leave empty to use this TV’s name, “%1$s”.
This device doesn’t accept controls from the TV
